player.seasonOutlook: The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

The rebuilding Dolphins are woefully lacking in talent on both sides of the football, and they're coming off a season in which they tied for 21st in fantasy points from the D/ST. An opening-week matchup against the Raiders could make them a viable streaming choice -- though that's directed more at you 12-, 14-team and Knockout managers ? but there's little else to like here, especially with one of the toughest overall schedules in the league ahead.

The seeds are here for the Cardinals to have a respectable pass defense -- Budda Baker, Josh Sweat and Will Johnson all return -- but a lot would need to go right for Nick Rallis' defense to become a fantasy force. As is, the Cardinals have one of the league's toughest D/ST schedules, largely due to their playing in last year's winningest division -- their three division rivals combined to go 38-13. But hey, they do have what could be a great fantasy-playoff schedule (NYJ, @NO, LV, from Weeks 15-17), if they show us anything early.
